scope: targeted web recovery for direct Cirsium manipulations of the three focal capitulum traits; not a systematic review; not-recovered means not found in this targeted search rather than proof of absence

recovered_Cirsium_context: Cirsium purpuratum has naturally nodding capitula and is visited predominantly by Bombus diversus, but the recovered study manipulates/display-assesses pollination rather than capitulum orientation
Cirsium pitcheri studies link head position and weevil infestation to seed production, but head position is architectural order rather than nodding-versus-erect orientation
orientation.closest_direct_manipulation: Cremanthodium campanulatum (Asteraceae): nodding-versus-artificially-erect capitula, pollen viability, pollinator preference and achene production
orientation.ceiling: direct Cirsium orientation causation remains untested

phyllary_posture.focal_Cirsium_context: Cirsium sieboldii naturally has appressed phyllaries yet documented bee, butterfly and hawkmoth visitors, constraining any claim that open/spreading phyllaries are required for legitimate visitor access
phyllary_posture.closest_direct_manipulation: Centaurea solstitialis (Cardueae): involucral-spine removal altered illegitimate Lepidoptera access and reduced filled seeds by 22% without increasing legitimate visitation frequency
phyllary_posture.independent_structural_analog: Pedicularis rex protective bract drainage increased seed predation and reduced final seed set without detectable pollinator discrimination
phyllary_posture.ceiling: direct Cirsium phyllary causation remains untested

direct_Cirsium_evidence: Willson, Anderson & Thomas 1983: experimentally occluding sticky bracteal exudates increased seed predation in C. discolor in Illinois but had no effect in C. flodmani in Minnesota
Thomas 2003: later C. discolor neutralization did not increase seed predators or reduce successful seed production
Thomas 2007: pollinators did not contact traps, several seed predators bypassed them, ants/aphids were deterred and some predatory arthropods used the sticky inflorescences
stickiness.current_leading_mechanism: guild-selective arthropod-community filtering with context-dependent benefit and an external cost prior
stickiness.ceiling: East-Asian JPN15/JPN06 causal effect remains untested without within-JPN15 neutralization and local community/fitness measurement

evidence_strength_order: stickiness: direct Cirsium manipulation and guild evidence
orientation: focal East-Asian transition ecology plus close Asteraceae manipulation
phyllary: focal repeated history plus close Cardueae manipulation
chapter2_stop_rule: No further broad public cause searching is justified for these three mappings unless a direct Cirsium orientation/phyllary manipulation or focal JPN15/JPN36 functional dataset is recovered. The next causal gain otherwise requires new focal manipulation/fitness data.
claim_boundary: This audit ranks evidence proximity and recovery status; it does not convert external analogs into Cirsium effects or prove adaptation.
